entries.lesson_core_move: Distinguish impulse area from ordinary signal amplitude when interpreting unit impulse terms in continuous-time signal constructions.

images.section_title: Interpreting Impulse Diagrams by Area Instead of Height
images.image_description: Time-axis diagram with three impulse stems at t=-2, t=1, and t=3. Each stem is centered at the time value and labeled with signed area values above the stem: 2 at t=-2, -1 at t=1, and 4 at t=3. Include a blank tick at t=0 with no stem so the student does not infer an impulse where none exists. Emphasize the area label as the symbolically meaningful quantity; do not encode height semantics or extra graph context.
missing_information: The style guide does not define an impulse-stem visual treatment with signed area labels.
new_visual_elements: Centered impulse stems at selected time points

images.report: Not covered: this slot needs an impulse-diagram/stem-plot treatment with signed area labels, and the current style guide only defines connected signal traces, graph-reading figures, and parameter annotations.

images.image_description: Time-axis diagram with four impulse stems at t=-3, t=-1, t=2, and t=4. Each stem is centered at the time value and labeled with signed area values above the stem: 1 at t=-3, -2 at t=-1, 3 at t=2, and 5 at t=4. Include a blank tick at t=1 with no stem so the student does not infer an impulse where none exists. Emphasize the area label as the symbolically meaningful quantity; do not encode height semantics or extra graph context.
